description.p: Seshat is a native Wayland file manager for Linux that works as a spatial, keyboard-first workspace. Opening a folder adds a panel instead of replacing the view, and every panel keeps its place, selection and settings while you move around.
Different paths through your folders become branches that are shown side by side, so you can work in several places at once and copy or move files between them.

ul.li: Persistent folder panels and branches, with shared folders shown once
Focus Mode expands the current folder without losing your place
Vim-style keys and a command line, with full mouse support
Select files across folders and branches, then copy or move them to one place
Copy, move, rename, Trash and restore with progress, cancellation and conflict resolution
Operations keep running when the window is closed, and other applications can follow them over D-Bus
